EIA crude and fuel inventory report: 
US crude oil inventories fell by 8.6 mb last week, the largest draw since February, partly reflecting production shut-ins caused by Hurricane Isaias. The disruption also contributed to a 0.3 mb/d decline in US crude production to 13.68 mb/d, the lowest since May. Meanwhile, gasoline stocks rose by 3.5 mb, while distillate inventories fell by 2.5 mb to 102.6 mb, the lowest seasonal level on record. Diesel production rose to a seasonal record of 5.2 mb/d while exports reached 1.4 mb/d, their highest seasonal level since 2013, highlighting strong overseas demand amid persistent global supply tightness.

Refinery crude runs rebounded to a fresh seasonal record, while four-week average implied gasoline demand declined by 100 kb/d, contrasting with a 200 kb/d increase in distillate demand. The report reinforces the divergence between gasoline where demand is easing and an increasingly tight diesel market, where strong domestic consumption and elevated exports continue to drain already depleted inventories.

US producer prices rose 6.3% y/y in September, the fastest pace in more than four years, primarily driven by a 10.8% jump in energy prices. Excluding food and energy, the index was 5% higher than a year ago, reaching levels last seen in early 2023 https://t.co/zmfxVAfyrm
